meta.scope: Etiquette and cultural concepts for nomads in Chiang Mai / Northern Thailand. Complements cultural_norms.json, beliefs_superstitions.json, ethnic_groups.json.
meta.note: Items with source=null are widely repeated practice without a fetched source here; marked low confidence for expert review.

etiquette.rule: Cover shoulders and knees; remove shoes before entering buildings and take off hats; keep voices low; no smoking, vaping or alcohol on temple grounds; never climb on, sit on or touch Buddha images.
do: Carry a scarf/sarong
Sit with feet tucked, soles pointing away from Buddha images and monks
Photograph discreetly, no flash
Small donation (e.g. 20 THB) is welcome
dont: Sit on monks' platforms or chairs

etiquette.rule: Some Northern temples and the Inthakhin city pillar shrine at Wat Chedi Luang bar women from specific sacred areas (sign: ห้ามสตรีเข้า / 'Ladies do not enter'). Local explanations combine Buddhist monastic rules with a belief that menstruation weakens protective yantra/relics.
do: Follow the sign without debate; men can go in and women can pay respect from outside
dont: Argue with temple staff or call it sexist on site
etiquette.app_note: If a female user asks why she can't enter, give the neutral cultural explanation, not a judgement.

etiquette.rule: Monks may not touch women or take items directly from a woman's hand.
do: Women: place an offering on a cloth or tray the monk sets down, or hand it via a man
Give monks the seat/space; lower your head slightly when passing
dont: Women: touch a monk or his robe, sit right next to him on public transport
Offer a monk food after noon (monks do not eat after midday) - app note, unverified
etiquette.needs_review: 'No food after noon' rule not from fetched source (well known Vinaya rule).

etiquette.rule: The head is the highest/most respected part of the body and feet the lowest; keep your head lower than monks and Buddha images, don't point feet at people or sacred objects.
do: Apologise if you accidentally touch someone's head or step over their things
dont: Point with your foot, rest feet on tables, step over people or food
etiquette.needs_review: Head-touching rule not explicit in fetched source; widely documented.

etiquette.rule: Palms together with a slight bow; junior person usually wais first. Full details in cultural_norms.json (wai_greeting).
do: Return a wai from an elder or vendor with a smile and nod or a chest-level wai
dont: Wai first to children or to service staff every time
etiquette.app_note: Pair Northern greeting 'sa-wat-di jao' (สะหวัดดีเจ้า, see kham_mueang_glossary.json) with a wai for elders.

etiquette.rule: Criticising, insulting or joking about the King, Queen, Heir-apparent or Regent is a crime under Criminal Code Art. 112 (3-15 years per count), also for foreigners and for online posts; not standing for the royal anthem has led to charges.
do: Stand for the royal anthem (e.g. in cinemas before films)
Treat royal portraits and banknotes (which carry the King's image) with respect
dont: Raise the monarchy as small talk or make jokes about it
Step on dropped banknotes/coins to stop them rolling
etiquette.app_note: If a user's message touches the monarchy, translate faithfully but add a cultural note advising caution; never generate commentary on the royal family.
etiquette.needs_review: Banknote-stepping example is common guidance, not in the fetched article.

etiquette.rule: No alcohol sales all day on Makha Bucha, Visakha Bucha, Asalha Bucha, Khao Phansa and Ok Phansa. Exempt: hotels, international airport terminals, licensed entertainment venues, bar-type venues in designated tourist zones, special events. Penalty up to 6 months and/or 10,000 THB. Loy Krathong and Songkran are NOT ban days.
do: Check festival_calendar.json alcohol_ban flag
Expect 7-Eleven and restaurants to refuse sales
dont: Ask a shop to 'make an exception'

etiquette.rule: Nationwide ban from 18:00 the day before voting to 18:00 on election day (national, and 24h for local elections in the area); applies to everyone including tourists.
do: Check Election Commission announcements for local elections
dont: Discuss or ask vendors about their vote

etiquette.rule: The national anthem plays at 08:00 and 18:00 in some public places (parks, stations); people stop and stand still.
do: Stop walking and stand quietly until it ends
etiquette.needs_review: No fetched source - widely known practice; expert please confirm and add source.

etiquette.rule: In Lanna belief, some transgressions (e.g. inappropriate physical contact or entering private rooms of a family's house) offend the family's ancestral spirits (phi pu ya) and require a forgiveness ritual/compensation.
do: Be restrained with physical affection towards a local partner in front of their family or in their home
dont: Enter bedrooms of a Northern family home uninvited
etiquette.needs_review: Expert: confirm scope of ผิดผี (compensation customs) and appropriate wording for foreigners dating locals.

etiquette.rule: Many Northern homes and businesses have a shrine for ancestor spirits (หิ้ง/หอผีปู่ย่า hing/ho phi pu ya) - often on the east wall above the sleeping area or a small house in a corner of the compound - plus the widespread spirit house for the land guardian. Offerings: flowers, incense, candles, drinks, food.
do: Leave offerings untouched
Ask before photographing a family shrine
dont: Lean on, sit near or use a spirit house as a shelf
etiquette.needs_review: Land-guardian spirit house term (ศาลพระภูมิ/ศาลเจ้าที่) not from a fetched Northern source.

etiquette.rule: Bargain politely and with a smile for crafts/clothes; food and marked prices are not bargained.
do: Carry small notes
Say 'mai phet' (not spicy) if needed; 'jay' for vegan/vegetarian (Chinese-style)
dont: Touch produce or food without gesture/permission
etiquette.needs_review: 'jay' = Chinese-Buddhist vegan (no garlic/onion too) - expert confirm nuance.

etiquette.rule: Use self-designations: Hmong (not 'Maeo'), Tai / Tai Yai for Shan, Karen/Pgaz K'nyau (Kariang/Yang are Thai exonyms), Tai Yuan / khon mueang for Northern Thais. Avoid 'hill tribe' as an identity label where possible (Thai official term is 'chao khao'). Full list in ethnic_groups.json.
do: Ask 'which village/where are you from?' rather than guessing someone's ethnicity
dont: Treat highland people as a photo attraction
Assume a highland person does not speak Thai
etiquette.needs_review: No single fetched source here; cross-check against ethnic_groups.json and expert.

lanna_concepts.thai: ขวัญ / สู่ขวัญ / ฮ้องขวัญ / เรียกขวัญ
lanna_concepts.meaning: Khwan is the vital soul-essence that can flee when a person is frightened or unsettled (ขวัญหนี 'khwan ni', ขวัญหาย). Soul-calling ceremonies (Lanna: ฮ้องขวัญ hong khwan; old phrase สู่ข้าวเอาขวัญ) call it back at life transitions: ordination, new house, weddings, farewells, welcoming guests, promotions, recovery from illness, graduations. Guests often receive white cotton strings tied on the wrist.
lanna_concepts.app_note: A vendor saying something about a user's 'khwan' after a fright or accident is a caring gesture; translate as 'your spirit/soul', not literally 'ghost'.
lanna_concepts.needs_review: Wrist-string tying (ผูกข้อมือ) not in fetched article; Lanna romanization of ขวัญหนี needs expert check.

lanna_concepts.meaning: Protective and place spirits: ผีปู่ย่า phi pu ya (family ancestors; shrine kept by the eldest daughter line, เก๊าผี), ผีเสื้อบ้าน phi suea ban (village guardian), ผีเสื้อเมือง phi suea mueang (city guardian, spirits of former rulers), ผีขุนน้ำ (headwater spirits), ผีดง/ผีดอย (forest/mountain spirits). Spirits are protectors, not only 'ghosts'.
lanna_concepts.app_note: Translate 'phi' by context: ancestor spirit / guardian spirit rather than 'ghost'.

lanna_concepts.meaning: A khantoke is a low round pedestal tray (~35 cm) used as a table for floor-seated meals with sticky rice (khao niao) and several dishes, used at weddings, housewarmings, temple fairs; the 'khantoke dinner' with dance shows for guests began in Chiang Mai in the 20th century.
lanna_concepts.app_note: Eat sticky rice with the right hand, rolling small balls; sit with feet tucked away from the tray.
lanna_concepts.needs_review: Right-hand/rolling etiquette and typical dishes (e.g. kaeng hang le, nam phrik ong, khaep mu) not in fetched source - check food files.

lanna_concepts.term: Lanna textiles: pha sin tin chok
lanna_concepts.thai: ผ้าซิ่นตีนจก
lanna_concepts.meaning: Hand-woven tube skirt of three parts: หัวซิ่น (waistband), ตัวซิ่น (body), ตีนซิ่น (decorated hem). 'Chok' (จก) is a discontinuous supplementary-weft technique picking up warp threads with a needle/quill; motifs include naga, hamsa (swans) and stupas. Mae Chaem district (Chiang Mai) is the best-known centre; a Tai Yuan tradition. Takes a long time to weave, so good pieces are expensive.
lanna_concepts.app_note: Good compliment topic with weavers/vendors; asking where a sin was woven is welcome.

lanna_concepts.thai: เดือนเหนือ
lanna_concepts.meaning: Lanna months run two ahead of Central Thai months, so Central month 12 = Lanna month 2 (Yi Peng = 'full moon of month two'); Inthakhin is 'month 8 in, month 9 out' (= Central 6-7).

good_topics.topic: Food: 'have you eaten?' (kin khao laeo ka / กิ๋นข้าวแล้วกา), favourite Northern dishes, what's in season
The current or next festival (Yi Peng, Songkran, Flower Festival) and how the family celebrates
Local crafts (umbrellas, silver, textiles) and where things were made
Weather/season: cool season, smoky season, rains
Learning a few Kham Mueang words - usually delights locals

avoid_or_careful.topic: Party politics, elections, protests - don't ask vendors how they vote
Criticising Buddhism, monks or Buddha images (Buddha-head decor/tattoos can offend)
Loud anger or public confrontation - losing face; stay calm and smiling when disputing prices
Framing highland/ethnic minorities as exotic, poor or 'primitive'

normal_questions_that_surprise_westerner.topic: Locals may ask your age, marital status, whether you have children, or what you earn/pay in rent; it is usually friendly curiosity to place you socially. A vague light answer is fine.
